editorial.headline: Repairing the Instruments That Keep Technical Systems Measured
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 33131 covers repair and maintenance for measuring, testing, navigation, and control equipment, nationally open to foreign ownership but blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 33131 is a technical maintenance activity, not a general repair bucket. The record places it around the repair and upkeep of equipment made in the measuring, testing, navigation, and control field: aircraft engine equipment, vehicle-emission testing equipment, meteorological instruments, physical, electrical, and chemical testing or inspection equipment, research or survey equipment, detection equipment, radiation monitoring equipment, and similar devices. In plain English, this is the workshop and service activity behind instruments that need to stay reliable because other decisions depend on their readings.

That scope matters because the activity is defined by the kind of equipment being maintained. It is concerned with apparatus used to measure, test, inspect, detect, navigate, control, survey, or monitor. A business registering this code should therefore be anchored in repair and maintenance work for those instruments, rather than in manufacturing, trading, consulting, or operating the measured systems themselves. The slim record also shows that the activity is open across the full Indonesian business-scale spectrum: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. In other words, the classification can sit behind a small specialist service operation or a larger technical-maintenance business, provided the activity remains within the stated repair-and-maintenance scope.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is clear. The PMA status is marked TERBUKA, and the maximum foreign ownership value is 100. That makes this a nationally foreign-open activity under the cited source, with no lower foreign-ownership ceiling appearing in the record. The honest national reading is therefore straightforward: for Indonesia as a whole, the record presents KBLI 33131 as open to PMA ownership up to 100%, across the listed business scales.

Bali changes the practical conclusion. The Bali-side status is marked BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO, and the record says the code is blocked in Bali because “OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026”. The moratorium rule is broader still: “Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA (island-wide, permanent)”. So the useful editorial lede is not that this code is nationally closed. It is not. The point is sharper: a foreign investor may see a 100% national PMA ceiling, but cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today under the Bali moratorium logic recorded here.
